full_judgment:
Md. Hassan Ameen J: This criminal appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 04-03-2003 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2840 of 1999 discharging the Rule obtained upon an application filed under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashment of G. R. Case No. 278 of 1999 arising out of Bogra P. S. Case No. 55 dated 14-03-1999 under Sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Bogra. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the respondent No. 2 lodged an FIR. alleging, inter-alia, that he deals in cement and the accused-appellant as proprietor and partner of M/S. H. M. Enterprise in course of business transaction purchase cement on credit on different dates in all worth Tk. 2,51,82,845/- and paid Tk. 1,1,90,77,076/- and there remained out standing amount of Tk. 61,05,769/-. Since inspite of repeated demands the accused appellant did not pay the outstanding amount there Was a salish on April 17, 1998 and the rein the accused appellant gave an undertaking to pay Tk. 61,00,000/- and further gave undertaking that on April 30, 1998 he would pay Tk. 25,00,000/- and on May 10, 1998 he would pay 6,00,000/- and the balance amount would be paid in 6 equal monthly installments. The accused-appellant failed to keep his commitment as per the undertaking and thereupon the informant through lawyer served a legal notice on May 11,1998 and the accused-appellant replied to the legal notice denying the payment of the amount due. On September 3, 1998 there was salish for the 2nd time and therein the accused-appellant admitted the money due from him and issued 3 post dated cheques of October 25, 1998, November 25, 4998, December 25, 1998 for an amount of Tk.  33,00,000/- and while the cheques were presented to the United Commercial Bank Ltd. Branch at Bogra on 25.10.1998, 14.1.1999 and  27.2.1999 the Bank returned the cheques with the remark "payment stopped by the drawer". The informant in the background of aforesaid facts contended the conduct of the accused-appellant and 3 others amount to criminal breach of trust and cheating. On the lodging of the FIR with the Bogra Police Station by the respondent No.  2, Bogra P.S. Case No. 55 dated 14.3.1999 was registered under Sections. 1406 and 420 of the Penal Code against the appellant and another. In connection with the aforesaid Bogra P.S. Case No. 55 dated 14.3.1999 in the Court of Magistrate 1st Class, Bogra (Zone-Ka) G.R. Case No.  278 of 1999 has been registered. 

 3. The appellant moved the High Court Division seeking quashment of the aforesaid G.R. Case contending that the transaction in connection with which Criminal Case has been filed was an ordinary business transaction and as such there was no criminal liability for the delay in the payment of the outstanding amount. It has also been contended that ingredients of Sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code are not attracted in respect of the transaction in the course of which the amount claimed by the respondent No. 2 has fallen due since there was no entrustment of any property and there was no initial deception to deceive the respondent No. 2. It was also the contention of the accused-appellant that the liability as has arisen out of ordinary business transaction, as such being a civil liability Criminal Case so registered is an abuse of process of the Court. 

 6. Mr. Khondakar Mahbub Hossain, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that even the facts stated in the F.I.R. is accepted as a whole it does not disclose any criminal offence under Sections 406/420 of the Penal Code as because the alleged facts in the F.I.R. disclosed a simple business transaction between the two parties and which calls for civil liability, which the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to consider in discharging the Rule and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division I failed to consider that the cement in question was taken on credit and part payment was made for the same on subsequent dates which categorically shows that the appellant had no initial intention to cheat the respondent No. 2 and mere failure to pay the outstanding dues does not come under the mischief of sections 406/420 of the Penal Code and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 9. In view of such facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the High Court Division has correctly assessed the materials on record and rightly discharged the Rule, which deserves no interference by this Division. In the result, the appeal is dismissed and thereby the impugned judgment and order is confirmed.
